/-!
# Littlewood conjectures

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littlewood_conjecture)
- [Bernard de Mathan and Olivier Teulié, *Problèmes diophantiens simultanés*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00605-003-0199-y)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

-- TODO(mercuris): This is a norm on ℝ/ℤ, show this?

namespace LittlewoodConjecture


/--
For any two real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$,
$$
  \liminf_{n\to\infty} n\||n\alpha\||\||n\beta\|| = 0
$$
where $\||x\|| := \min(|x - \lfloor x \rfloor|, |x - \lceil x \rceil|)$ is the distance
to the nearest integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem littlewood_conjecture (α β : ℝ) :
    atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ n * distToNearestInt (n * α) * distToNearestInt (n * β)) = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
For real number $\alpha$ and prime $p$,
$$
  \liminf\_{n \to\infty} n |n|\_{p}\||n\alpha\|| = 0
$$
where $\||x\|| := \min(|x - \lfloor x \rfloor|, |x - \lceil x \rceil|)$ is the distance
to the nearest integer, and $|x|\_{p}$ is the $p$-adic norm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem padic_littlewood_conjecture (α : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    atTop.liminf (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ n * padicNorm p n * distToNearestInt (n * α)) = 0 := by
  sorry

end LittlewoodConjecture

reformulations.difference: Lean states liminf as n tends to infinity over ℕ, whereas Wikipedia’s p-adic section and equation (1.4) of arXiv:1405.5545 state infimum over positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write a(n)=n|n|ₚ‖nα‖. The sequence is nonnegative, and a(p^k)≤1/2, so the real-valued liminf has no unbounded-set default issue. For positive integers k,n, multiplicativity of the p-adic norm, |k|ₚ≤1, and ‖kx‖≤k‖x‖ give a(kn)≤k²a(n). If the positive-index infimum is zero, then for ε>0 and any N, choose k=N+1 and n≥1 with a(n)<ε/k². Consequently kn≥N and a(kn)<ε, proving liminf zero. Conversely, liminf zero supplies positive-index values below every ε>0. The index n=0 is ignored by atTop. The exact equivalence was proved independently in /workspace/review/liminf_checks.lean.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Littlewood_conjecture — statements, elementary cases, variants, and current status.
https://doi.org/10.1007/s00605-003-0199-y — de Mathan and Teulié, Problèmes diophantiens simultanés; publisher abstract and bibliographic information (full text paywalled).
https://pmb.centre-mersenne.org/articles/10.5802/pmb.1/ — Bugeaud, Around the Littlewood conjecture in Diophantine approximation; abstract and bibliography.

https://arxiv.org/e-print/1405.5545 — Badziahin, Bugeaud, Einsiedler, and Kleinbock, On the complexity of a putative counterexample to the p-adic Littlewood conjecture; LaTeX source, Introduction, equations (1.1)–(1.4), and §2.3.
review.notes: Both declarations were checked. The cited Wikipedia page still records both conjectures as open. Scratch proofs verified the nearest-integer floor/ceiling formula, nonnegativity and frequent upper bounds for both sequences, the classical epsilon/arbitrarily-large-index characterization, and the p-adic infimum equivalence. The equivalence proofs depend only on standard Lean axioms, not on either conjecture or sorryAx. Boundary tests covered zero, integers, half-integers, negative inputs, and small p-adic norm values. The original de Mathan–Teulié full text was inaccessible, but its formulation was corroborated by the cited Wikipedia page and the explicit primary-literature statement in arXiv:1405.5545. All experiments were kept under /workspace/review; the reviewed file was unchanged.
